label: September 1915
headline: Loos and Champagne
deck: The Allies attack on two fronts; the British use gas for the first time
caption: A grey cloud drifts from the British trenches towards the slag heaps of Loos
body: On 25 September the Allies open their greatest offensive of the year. In Champagne the French attack on a front of some fifteen miles after a bombardment of three days, and their first rush carries the German forward trenches. Behind them a second line, hidden on the reverse slopes, stops the advance. By the time it stops in October it has cost the French some 145,000 men.

In Artois the British attack at Loos, among pitheads and slag heaps, and release gas for the first time; in places it drifts back into their own trenches. Scottish battalions take Loos village and Hill 70, but the reserves arrive too late and too tired, and on the second day they are cut down before the German wire.
In Russia the Tsar has taken personal command of his armies on 5 September, and the great retreat comes to an end.
briefs: Zeppelins bomb the City of London on 8 September
British and Indian troops take Kut al-Amara on the Tigris
